name: SN2 hydrolysis of alkyl bromide
outcome: Typically 60-90%; alcohol with inversion at stereogenic centers.
notes: Best for methyl and primary bromides; inversion occurs at a stereogenic center.

name: SN2 hydrolysis of alkyl chloride
outcome: Typically 50-85%; alcohol with inversion at stereogenic centers.
notes: Primary chlorides react most reliably; hindered substrates favor elimination.

name: SN1 solvolysis to tertiary alcohol
outcome: Typically 40-80%; tertiary alcohol with racemization and rearrangement risk.
notes: A stable tertiary carbocation enables solvolysis; rearrangement and racemization are possible.

name: Cyanide substitution
outcome: Typically 60-90%; nitrile with one additional carbon.
notes: Adds one carbon and works best on unhindered alkyl halides.

name: Azide substitution
notes: Alkyl azides are useful masked amines; avoid concentrating low-molecular-weight azides.

name: Ammonolysis of alkyl bromide
outcome: Typically 40-75%; primary amine, with overalkylation possible.
notes: Excess ammonia suppresses over-alkylation of the primary amine product.

name: Williamson ether synthesis
outcome: Typically 60-95%; unsymmetrical ether by SN2 substitution.
notes: Use a primary alkyl halide to minimize competing E2 elimination.

name: Gabriel amine synthesis
notes: Provides primary amines without over-alkylation; unsuitable for aryl or tertiary halides.

name: Tosylation of alcohol
outcome: Typically 75-98%; sulfonate ester with retention at carbon.
notes: Converts the hydroxyl group into a good leaving group without breaking the C-O bond.

name: Finkelstein halide exchange
outcome: Typically 60-95%; alkyl iodide as NaCl precipitates.
notes: Most effective for primary substrates; secondary substrates react more slowly and tertiary substrates eliminate.

name: SN2 thioether synthesis
outcome: Typically 65-95%; thioether with inversion at stereogenic electrophiles.
notes: Thiolate is strongly nucleophilic; exclude oxidants to limit disulfide formation.

name: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution by phenoxide
outcome: Typically 55-90%; diaryl ether when electron-withdrawing groups activate the aryl fluoride.
notes: Classical addition-elimination SNAr requires ortho or para electron-withdrawing activation; unactivated aryl halides are poor substrates.
